---
title: "Assignment 2 — From structure to energy"
---

In Laboratory 2 we will perform our first electronic-structure calculations
with **CRYSTAL23**. We will continue to use MgO (periclase), so that the
structure remains simple while we concentrate on a new question:

> **When can we trust a calculated energy numerically?**

You are not expected to learn electronic-structure theory or the CRYSTAL input
language in full. The aim is to understand the logic of a first-principles
calculation, recognize the important parts of an input and output file, and
perform a controlled convergence test.

## Before the laboratory

Read:

- **Laboratory 2 — From structure to energy**;
- the short **CRYSTAL input and output field guide**;
- the **CluMiner** quick reference.

Then update your personal workspace:

```bash
update-course
```

and create the Laboratory 2 working directory:

```bash
start-lab 02
```

Open:

```text
work/lab02/
```

You should find:

```text
01-first-scf.ipynb
02-kpoint-convergence.ipynb
inputs/
outputs/
reference-results/
```

The first notebook is guided. The second contains the convergence activity and
your answers.

::: {.callout-important}
## Keep the numerical experiment controlled

During the convergence test you will change **only the SHRINK factor**.

The MgO structure, basis set, exchange-correlation functional, integral
thresholds, SCF convergence threshold and computational resources must remain
unchanged.
:::

## Calculation resources

For every CRYSTAL calculation in this laboratory use:

```bash
cluminer-crystal INPUT.d12 --cores-per-node 2 --threads 2
```

This corresponds to one MPI rank using two OpenMP threads on two physical CPU
cores. Do not request more resources unless instructed.

## What you will produce

By the end of the activity you should have:

- CRYSTAL outputs for SHRINK values 2–9;
- a table containing the reciprocal-space sampling, total energy and timings;
- energy-difference values in both hartree and kJ mol$^{-1}$;
- convergence and computational-cost plots;
- a justified choice of the SHRINK value to use in subsequent MgO calculations.

No separate report is required. Your answers remain in the notebook.
